Steps: Open Executive overview with default filters. Compare dates and total to reports/quality.json.
Expected result: 24 complete months and the complete-population count agree. Partial month is excluded.

Steps: Read the partial-month note and compare its count to quality.json partial.complaints.
Expected result: Partial count agrees and is not added to the main count.

Steps: Select Credit card only. Compare the displayed total with a matching SQL count.
Expected result: Only Credit card records and totals appear.

Steps: Remove both selected products in Executive overview.
Expected result: Count is zero, timely rate is n.a., and the page remains usable.

Steps: Select a company, a state and a product. Download the matching records.
Expected result: Every exported row satisfies all three selections.

Steps: Select Jan 1 through Jan 31 of a source year. Compare export minimum/maximum and count with SQL.
Expected result: All eligible Jan 1 and Jan 31 records are included; February records are excluded.

Steps: On Response quality, divide Timely Yes by Known Status. Compare with the displayed percentage.
Expected result: Yes/(Yes+No) agrees to display precision; unknown records do not enter denominator.

Steps: Run the documented all-unknown fixture and inspect the result.
Expected result: Timely rate is unavailable, not zero or 100%.

Steps: Execute missing-month fixture with Jan and March records only.
Expected result: February remains zero and March percentage change is unavailable after a zero baseline.

Steps: Use three complete displayed months; manually average their counts.
Expected result: Third-month rolling mean agrees; first two rolling values are unavailable.

Steps: Select the last two complete months. Sum every issue change in the download.
Expected result: Sum equals comparison-month total less baseline total; waterfall Other issues preserves equality.

Steps: Run fixture containing one issue only in January and another only in March.
Expected result: Both issues appear; the new issue has no percentage baseline.

Steps: Execute a fixture with counts 4 and 5; set minimum 4 and growth 25%. Repeat with minimum 5.
Expected result: First result is flagged; second is not.

Steps: Open Review planning. Download its queue and inspect source timeliness for every ID.
Expected result: Every row is No, ordered newest date then ID; no inferred unresolved status.

Steps: Set two reviewers, 20 hours, 30 minutes and 75% productive time.
Expected result: Weekly capacity is 60 reviews.

Steps: Set Reviewers to zero on Review planning.
Expected result: Capacity is zero and all selected records remain.

Steps: Choose inputs with capacity greater than the queue count.
Expected result: Remaining is zero, never negative.

Steps: Open the workbook. Compare Overview count and rate to quality.json complete values.
Expected result: Counts agree exactly; rate agrees to display precision.

Steps: Change Analysis product selector and Capacity reviewer count. Restore defaults afterward.
Expected result: Linked counts/charts and capacity results recalculate; source observations remain unchanged.

Steps: Inspect a Detail product and its mapped review team; change the matching Lookups team in a disposable copy.
Expected result: XLOOKUP updates the matching rows; mapping is labeled simulated.

Steps: Inspect test status, actual result, reviewer and sign-off fields.
Expected result: Unexecuted human tests remain Not run; automated evidence is separately identified.

Steps: Apply filters, download CSV, count rows and compare to the displayed matching count.
Expected result: Count and IDs agree; formula-like strings are escaped.

Steps: In a disposable fixture, duplicate an ID or change a source hash. Run validation.
Expected result: Build fails with a clear contract message; it does not silently publish changed totals.

Steps: Open all five workspaces at normal browser size; inspect controls, captions and empty states.
Expected result: Navigation works; data definitions and context are visible; no application exceptions.
